review_summary: The differential correctly identifies diabetic nephropathy as the dominant process and includes reasonable secondary contributors. Probability weighting needs adjustment, and several critical laboratory abnormalities (bilirubinuria, ketonuria, glucosuria) lack sufficient supporting data. Additional testing (BP measurement, medication review, serum glucose/ketones, tubular labs) is required to clarify secondary diagnoses and address unexplained findings.
